title: STALEY SENTENCED
full_story:
Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip M. Givens announced that Andrew J. Staley, 45, of Flora, was sentenced to time in the Illinois Department of Corrections on Wednesday, in Clay County Circuit Court for the offenses of Indecent Solicitation of a Child, a Class 3 Felony, and Grooming, a Class 4 Felony.

The charges alleged that between July 1st, and July 22nd, Staley solicited one whom he believed to be a minor child to perform an act of sexual penetration or sexual conduct through an on-line service.  Staley pled guilty to Indecent Solicitation of a Child and was sentenced to 7 years to the Illinois Department of Corrections.  He also pled guilty to Grooming and was sentenced to 4 years to the Illinois Department of Corrections.  The sentences will run concurrently and will have a 6-month period of Mandatory Supervised Release.  Staley will also be required to register as a Sex Offender and abide by the terms and conditions of the Illinois Sex Offender Registration Act.

The investigation was conducted by Predator Poachers and the Flora Police Department.  State’s Attorney Phillip Givens said: “I am grateful for the individuals who led the investigation with Predator Poachers.  This should serve as an example of how access to online chat rooms for minors can be dangerous.  Thankfully this situation did not involve an actual minor child.  Please be aware of who your children are talking to online.  My office will continue to work with law enforcement and others to keep predators out of our community.”

title: WEST NILE POSITIVE IN CLAY COUNTY
full_story:
Clay County Health Department confirmed the second West Nile virus (WNV) positive mosquito sample of the 2026 season in Clay County.  The positive sample was collected in Clay City on Wednesday and was confirmed through routine testing.

Confirmation of a WNV positive mosquito sample means that the virus is circulating in the community and there is a heightened risk of infection for humans.  Residents are urged to take the necessary precautions to protect themselves from mosquito bites.  It is important to remember the three R’s – reduce your exposure to mosquitoes, repel them by wearing insect repellant, and report areas where mosquitoes typically breed.

WNV is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected mosquito.  Mosquitoes pick up the virus by feeding on infected birds.  The illness is not spread from person-to-person.  Most people infected with West Nile virus show no symptoms.  However, some people may experience fever, nausea, headache, and muscle aches.  Symptoms may last from a few days to a few weeks.  In rare cases, severe illness including meningitis or encephalitis, or even death, can occur.  People older than 50 are at higher risk for severe illness from West Nile virus.

Because WNV generally appears and spreads in Illinois mosquito populations as early as two to six weeks before it is transmitted to humans, monitoring the mosquito populations in our communities helps us predict when humans will be at risk for WNV infection.  Surveillance activities in Clay County include laboratory tests on mosquito batches and responding to concerns of mosquito production sites.

If you would like more information on West Nile virus, contact the Clay County Health Department at 662-4406 or visit the website www.healthdept.org.

title: FLORA HYDRANT FLUSHING
full_story:
The City of Flora Water Department will have its fire hydrant flushing program on Wednesday, August 26th and 27th from 7:30 am until approximately 3:30 pm.

Although it may appear to be a waste of water, the process is part of a routine maintenance program necessary to maintain the integrity of the water system, allowing the city to continue to deliver the highest quality water possible to our customers.  As a result of the line flushing process, residents in the immediate vicinity of the work may experience temporary discoloration of their water.  This discoloration consists primarily of harmless silt and air and does not affect the safety of the water.

If you experience discoloration in your water after crews have been flushing in your neighborhood, clear the pipes in your home by running all water faucets for a few minutes.  Washing light colored laundry is not recommended during this period.  The same philosophy of water line preventive maintenance is one that you should use in your own home to ensure the quality of water inside your home.  Your home’s water heater should be drained and flushed on a regular basis, according to manufacturers’ recommendations, to keep it working effectively and efficiently.

title: HEALTH DEPARTMENT GRANT
full_story:
At the beginning of August, Clay County Health Department was named a recipient of a $5,000 Community Grant from the Illinois State Dental Society Foundation (ISDSF).

The ISDS Foundation’s 2026 grants reflect a commitment to serving Illinois’ most vulnerable populations, children, seniors, refugees, people with disabilities, and the uninsured.  By supporting these innovative programs and essential services, the Foundation helps ensure brighter, healthier smiles across the state.

This year, the Illinois State Dental Society Foundation awarded $125,000 in community grants to 20 nonprofit organizations dedicated to expanding access to dental care across the state.  The 2026 grants support projects ranging from mobile clinics and emergency care vouchers to specialized programs for the elderly, children, refugees, and people with disabilities.

This community grant received will further help the Clay County Health Department’s continuation and expansion of services offered at their mobile adult dental clinics.  At these adult dental clinics, the Health Department offers exams, cleanings and fluoride treatments, intraoral imaging, and SDF treatment, if needed.  In the future, CCHD hopes to include dental x-rays to services offered.  To qualify for these clinics, individuals must: Live in Clay County or receive WIC services through CCHD, be age 20 or older, have Medicaid or no insurance, be income eligible, and have not seen the dentist in the past year.

Since the start of these dental clinics, the health department has been able to provide dental services to over 150 individuals who may not have received care otherwise.

title: IECC BOARD
full_story:
The Illinois Eastern Community College District Board approved policies, budgets, agreements, and staffing decisions at its Monday night meeting.

The Fiscal Year 2027 Tentative Budget and accompanying Budget Resolution were approved.  The budget reflects anticipated revenues and expenditures for the upcoming fiscal year, including $20.67 million in planned capital outlay.  A public hearing and final budget adoption are scheduled for September 15th, at Lincoln Trail College.

The Board approved the 2026 IECC Program Review Report, which evaluates career and technical programs, academic disciplines, and student support services based on quality, cost, need, equity, and performance. The review helps identify opportunities for curriculum updates, resource needs, and continued improvement of programs and services.

A clinical education agreement with the University of Southern Indiana’s Kinney College of Nursing and Health Professions was approved, providing opportunities for its nursing students to complete required practical learning and clinical experiences at IECC facilities.

The Board declared approximately 1.21 acres of District-owned property adjacent to Frontier Community College unnecessary for Community College purposes and authorized its sale.  The property will be marketed for student housing development, with conditions requiring the purchaser to use the property for student housing and begin construction within three months of closing.

Approval of employment was given for Destiny Nesler as Physical Therapy Assistant Instructor, at WVC; Gabriell Weber as TRIO Upward Bound Academic Counselor, at WVC; Sydney Miller as TRIO Upward Bound Academic Counselor, at LTC; Sam Romershausen as Information Systems Technician, at WVC; Luis Rodriguez as Head Men’s & Women’s Soccer Coach, at LTC; and Joe Hunt as O&M Team Lead, at OCC, all effective August 24th.

The next regular meeting of the Board of Trustees will be Tuesday, September 15th, at 6:15 pm at Wabash Valley College, Mt. Carmel.

title: MARSHALS ARREST
full_story:
Thursday, the US Marshals Service Southern District of Illinois Great Lakes Regional Fugitive Task Force (USMS-GLTF) located and apprehended a wanted fugitive residing in Belleville.

Eric Wayne Hubert, 23, had active felony arrest warrants in Dallas County, Texas for two separate murders.  His charges stem from two shooting incidents.  In September 2024, Hubert was charged in Dallas County, Texas for the murder of an individual who died following a firearm shooting.  Hubert was then released on bond.  According to court documents, in April 2026, Hubert allegedly removed his ankle monitor in violation of his bond conditions.

Hubert is also suspected to have engaged in a deadly shooting on North Masters Drive in Dallas, Texas on June 9th.  During the incident, Hubert and two other masked individuals allegedly shot semi-automatic rifles at numerous individuals in front of a store.  One individual was killed.  Hubert then fled Texas to Illinois.

On Thursday, members of the USMS-GLTF responded to Hubert’s residence in Belleville and arrested him without incident.  Hubert was transported to St. Clair County Jail for booking, pending his extradition to Texas.

title: TONTI TRAIN WRECK REMAINS IDENTIFIED
full_story:
Two people whose remains had gone unidentified since the 1971 Tonti train wreck have been identified as two members of the same family, Katherine Marcelin and Gladys “Gigi” Adams, bringing long-awaited answers to their surviving family after 55 years.  Those involved in the project were surprised to learn during the initial investigation that the grave may have contained more than one person.

The effort began in early 2025 when Henry Morton approached the City of Salem with the idea of revisiting the decades-old case.  Recognizing the project’s importance and the possibilities created by advances in DNA analysis and forensic genetic genealogy, the City worked with Morton to bring together the right partners and determine whether the unidentified remains could finally be identified.

On June 12, 2025, the unidentified remains were exhumed so DNA samples could be collected for forensic analysis.  As the investigation progressed, they made an unexpected discovery.  What had long been believed to be the remains of one unidentified person was determined to include the remains of two separate individuals.

The identifications resulted from a collaborative effort involving college student Henry Morton, the City of Salem, Marion County Coroner Claude Howell, the DNA Doe Project, forensic anthropologists, Crouse Funeral Home, Merz Vault Company, and others who contributed to the project.

title: EGG RECALL
full_story:
The Food and Drug Administration upgraded an egg recall to the highest risk level.  The FDA declared it a Class One recall on Wednesday citing the possibility that consuming the eggs could cause serious health consequences or death.

The FDA’s upgraded risk classification comes three weeks after Midwest Poultry Services initiated a recall of the approximately 19 million affected eggs, according to a company announcement shared on the FDA website July 22nd.

The eggs were produced at farms in Texas between June 6th and July 3rd, and the cartons show sell-by or best-by dates between July 20th, and August 17th.  They were distributed to Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Texas.

Samples collected at the farms tested positive for salmonella, and genetic sequencing found that some matched the strain responsible for the outbreak, according to the FDA.

However, in a July 24th update from the FDA, the agency said that Midwest Poultry Services “does not account for all the illnesses in this outbreak.”  It did not identify any additional known origins.

Consumers who may have purchased contaminated products have been advised by the FDA to either throw them away or return them for a refund at the place of purchase.  The recalled eggs were sold under Country Morning, Cal-Maine Sunups, Brookshire’s, Simple Truth, and Kroger brand names.  Potentially contaminated products can be identified by the codes P-1950 or 0840962 with a Julian date between 157 and 184.

According to the latest update, nearly 98 people have been sickened across 17 states, with 26 hospitalizations. No deaths have been reported.
